regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: This is the exact flow_requirement:near_wake volume and it currently has configured_volume_coverage 0.0, which is the sole reason scenario_screen is rejected. Level 3 gives h = 0.1305/2^3 = 0.0163 m = 0.39x the required max_cell_axis_span 0.04225 m (= H/8), so the recirculating bubble, base shear layers and C-pillar vortices get ~2.6x more cells across the shear layer than level 2 would allow and the box retains margin against the native 1.5x p95 tolerance. Level 3 equals the global surface level, so no hanging-node cliff is created where the wake box meets the body surface, and the box is inside the domain (domain extends to x ~ 5.12, y +/-1.14, z from about -0.51 upward).

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Exact flow_requirement:far_wake volume, also at configured_volume_coverage 0.0. The region contains 0 geometry samples and finite_fluid_gap_fraction 0.0, so it is pure off-body fluid that only transports the velocity deficit and residual shear. Level 2 gives h = 0.0326 m = 0.39x the required 0.0845 m (= H/4); level 1 (0.0653 m) would pass the nominal limit but with only 1.29x margin and coarser box-boundary cells, while the extra cost of level 2 is small (~26k cells) relative to the 2,000,000 budget, so level 2 is the better cost/robustness trade for a downstream transport zone.

regions.name: flow_base_shear
regions.why: Targets the shear-layer/C-pillar-vortex generation region at the slant and base periphery, which is the source term of flow_requirement:near_wake ('rear separation, shear layers and recirculating vehicle wake'). The existing physical_refinement_bands stop at 0.0979 m from the wall (level 2 = 0.0326 m) while the wake box is 0.0163 m; starting refinement only at x = 0.944 would place a cell-size step of 2x across the separation origin, degrading shear-layer thickness and vortex-core resolution exactly where they are set. The box uses the same transverse/vertical bounds as the near-wake box so the two refined volumes are contiguous over x = 0.62-1.988 with no internal step; solid cells inside the body footprint are discarded by snappy, so the real added volume is only the ~0.05-0.08 m3 of fluid above, beside and below the base (about 19k cells). Level 3 is within +2 of the global surface level 3.

advisor.hypothesis: The surface mesh is already deterministic-certified (finest 0.0163 m, unresolved_feature_fraction 0.0, 42,939 measured edges with only 1.7% above the 60 deg layer feature angle), so the single blocking defect is off-body: scenario_screen reports configured_volume_coverage = 0.0 for BOTH flow_requirement:near_wake and flow_requirement:far_wake, i.e. no off-body box exists at all. The defect is a missing-resolution defect, not a geometry or layer defect. Measured scales make the correct levels unambiguous: background h = 0.1305 m, global surface cell = 0.0163 m (level 3), so level 3 = 0.0163 m, level 2 = 0.0326 m, level 1 = 0.0653 m. near_wake demands max_cell_axis_span 0.04225 m (= H/8, H = 0.338 m) => level >= 2, choose level 3 for margin against the 1.5x p95 tolerance. far_wake demands 0.0845 m (= H/4) => level >= 1, choose level 2 (0.0326 m ~ 0.39x limit, still cheap) because the far wake carries only the transported velocity deficit, not new shear production. The near-wake query box returned 191 ray samples with dihedral p95 = 90 deg, i.e. the box is bounded by the flat rear/leg release edges rather than being buried in solid; the far-wake box returned 0 geometry samples and finite_fluid_gap_fraction 0.0, confirming it is genuinely off-body fluid and needs pure cell-size refinement, no snap/layer work. The third mechanism: the near-wake requirement's own stated mechanism is "rear separation, shear layers and recirculating vehicle wake". In a 25-deg slant-back Ahmed-type body the separating shear layer and the C-pillar vortices are generated at the slant/base periphery (x ~ 0.62-0.944), and snappyHexMesh refinement is not conformal: if boxes start exactly at x = 0.944 there is a cell-size cliff (0.0326 m -> 0.0163 m) laid across the separation origin, which is a known source of spurious wake structure and of smeared shear-layer thickness. A bounded level-3 box over the generation region keeps resolution continuous from the wall (level 3) through the shear layer and into the wake box, at low cost.
alternatives: Use refinement_bands (inner_distance 0.032625 m at level 3, outer_distance 0.097875 m at level 2) alone to cover the wake - rejected: a surface-distance shell cannot reach 1.0-3.1 m downstream, so configured_volume_coverage would stay 0.0 and the screen would still fail.

Raise base_cells / surface_level globally to buy wake resolution - rejected: certification already passes with unresolved_feature_fraction 0.0, and a global level change multiplies the 46k layer cells and the four level-5 leg feature boxes, risking the 2,000,000 cell gate with no geometric benefit.

Set the near-wake box to level 2 only (0.0326 m, still under the 0.04225 m requirement) - viable and half the cells, but leaves only 1.30x margin against the 1.5x p95 tolerance and puts only ~1 cell across the shear layer, so I keep level 3 as primary and note level 2 as the fallback if the native count gate is approached.

Set the far-wake box to level 1 (0.0653 m <= 0.0845 m) - rejected as primary: only 1.29x margin and box-boundary cells remain coarser than the box level, so a p95 measurement could fail; level 2 costs only ~26k cells.

Shrink n_surface_layers because the 0.0184 m layer stack exceeds the 0.0163 m surface cell - rejected for now: layer_shortfall/coverage evidence is absent before the first mesh, and max_face_thickness_ratio is inactive for absolute heights; a speculative layer edit would trade a certain defect for an unmeasured one.
counterevidence: scenario_screen.accepted is false only because configured off-body boxes are absent; it is NOT a native cell-size failure, and native cell measurement is still required after meshing - passing this screen does not prove wake resolution.

Both requirement boxes are labelled evidence_status = unvalidated_physical_hypothesis: their position comes from a bounded dimensionless prior, so the boxes refine a hypothesised wake, not a measured one; no separation point, vortex trajectory or wake recovery has been observed here.

The scenario declares boundary_environment = unbounded_single_phase and states stationary/moving-ground conditions are not reproduced, so I deliberately add no ground refinement and make no underbody/ground-clearance refinement claim.

initial_certification forecast is unvalidated and conservative (409k cells after these boxes vs 2,000,000 budget); the added level-3 near wake (0.269 m3) and base-shear (0.084 m3) boxes and level-2 far wake (0.890 m3) are the dominant new cost and the real native count is a hard gate.

No native layer, snap or quality defect has been measured yet, so this plan deliberately touches only off-body cell size and leaves layers/snap/features at their certified baseline; refinement does not cure extrusion defects and can introduce transition defects at box boundaries.
advisor.expected_change: scenario_screen.configured_volume_coverage should move 0.0 -> 1.0 for flow_requirement:near_wake and -> ~1.0 for flow_requirement:far_wake with accepted = true (preview already shows exactly this). Inside the near-wake box the available cell axis span becomes 0.0163 m against the 0.04225 m requirement (ratio 0.39) and inside the far-wake box 0.0326 m against 0.0845 m (ratio 0.39), so even a 1.5x p95 tolerance leaves headroom, versus the current condition where the wake sits in 0.0653-0.1305 m background cells. Forecast cell count rises from ~249k to ~409k of the 2,000,000 budget. Uncertainty: the forecast is uncalibrated; the native count, native p95 cell span, and any new non-orthogonality/skewness introduced at the three box transitions are unknown until snappyHexMesh and checkMesh run. No statement is made about flow convergence, drag accuracy or wake physics - the boxes only make the hypothesised wake region resolvable.
